Patient’s initial 12-lead ECG
The 12-lead ECG with correct limb leads placement shows sinus rhythm with complete right bundle branch block

ECG at presentation ECG on presentation shows a heart rate of 70 beats per minute. P waves are small in amplitude with a frontal P wave axis of about +120°. P waves are inverted in all the precordial leads. QRS complexes are narrow with a frontal axis of +225°, qR pattern in lead V1 and Qr in V6. T wave inversion is seen in all the precordial leads.
Repeat ECG Repeat ECG shows sinus rhythm at 80 beats per minute, PR interval 110 ms, narrow QRS with a normal frontal axis, no abnormal q waves and no significant ST-T abnormalities.

Panel A - Diagrammatic representation of normal Einthoven's triangle with the three standard limb leads and the imaginary position of precordial leads Panel B - Incorrect lead connections due to cable reversal leading to altered Wilson central terminal and uninterpretable electrocardiogram.
